title: Coral and the Thorn
premise: Casper Ashgrove, exiled for a storm they never meant to call, has survived seven quiet years in Greyhollow by selling charms too small to hang them. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into their hands, Casper learns the king of Veyland is no longer the man who banished them—he is a hollowed vessel, and the thing wearing his crown is hunting every storm-caller left alive, including Casper's lost sister. Guided by Wren, a disgraced royal guard with her own debts to pay, Casper must reach the capital before the solstice binding ritual makes the usurper immortal. In the end, Casper chooses to unbind their own exile-oath and take the storm back into themselves, destroying the crown-thing at the cost of their magic—and finding, at last, that belonging was never something power could buy.
about_author: C. M. Crane is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped coastlines before turning to mapping impossible ones. They write fantasy about people who carry too much weather inside them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Charms
chapters.summary: In Greyhollow's rain-slick market, Casper sells a luck-charm to a frightened child while hiding their true gift from the city's magic-sniffing wardens. A bleeding stranger collapses at their stall, pressing a map and a broken signet ring into Casper's hands with a warning: 'He knows your name now.' POV: Casper. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of invisibility shattering.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Fleeing wardens, Casper teams up with Wren, the disgraced guard sent to arrest them who defects instead. The map reveals itself as a living document, tracing ley-lines toward the capital and showing visions of the king—hollow-eyed, whispering in two voices. Casper recognizes their sister's handwriting on its margins. POV: alternating Casper and Wren. Emotional beat: reluctant trust kindling between two people running from duty.

chapters.title: The Solstice Crown
chapters.summary: Reaching the capital during the solstice festival, Casper infiltrates the palace and finds their sister alive but bound as the crown-thing's anchor. The usurper offers Casper a bargain: their sister's freedom for the storm-magic it needs to complete its immortality. Wren is captured buying time. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: love against duty made flesh—the temptation to trade everything for one person.

chapters.title: Stormcaller's Oath
chapters.summary: At the binding ritual, Casper refuses the bargain and instead calls the storm they were exiled for, unbinding their oath to feed it. The crown-thing, starved of an unwilling vessel, unravels; the king wakes, and Casper's sister is freed. Magicless and ordinary, Casper stays in a kingdom that finally says their name without fear. POV: Casper, closing with Wren beside them. Emotional beat: belonging won not through power, but sacrifice.
